title: Convergence of repeated-pole rational approximation of the exponential on infinite sectors
summary: For $h>0$, degree $m\ge0$, $0\leβ 0$, let $Σ_β=\{re^{iθ}:r\ge0,\ |θ|\leβ/2\}$ and let $E_{m,β}(q)$ denote the best uniform error for approximating $e^{-hz}$ on $Σ_β$ by rational functions whose only possible finite pole is $s=-q/h$, with multiplicity at most $m$. For the linear scaling $q=αm$ with a fixed $α>0$, a Möbius map reduces the problem to polynomial approximation on a compact lens. Write $γ_β=2-β/π$ and let $α_c(γ_β)$ denote the saddle-coalescence threshold. For $0<α<α_c(γ_β)$, let $H_β(α)\in(0,1)$ be the exponential of the real saddle action.
